scope.summary: This standard specifies the requirements, sampling guidelines, and testing methods for Polyaluminium Chloride (PAC) used in water purification (including drinking water treatment) and industrial wastewater processing. It covers both Liquid and Powder forms of PAC, which are further divided into Medium Basicity and High Basicity types.

amendment_slips.description: Substitutes specific test parameters in Table 1 and updates the standard BIS Certification marking clause to align with the BIS Conformity Assessment Regulations, 2018.
Incorporates minor technical and chemical parameter adjustments.

Revises the physical description for Liquid PAC (colourless to pale yellow, hazy to transparent liquid) and Powder PAC (pale yellow powder). It also substitutes the title of Annex C from 'Long Term Protection Test' to 'Determination of Chloride Test'.

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Poly Aluminium Chloride (Quality Control) Order, 2019' issued by the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, Government of India, all Polyaluminium Chloride manufactured, imported, distributed, or sold in India must carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) to be legally distributed in the domestic market. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to industrial water treatment compounds as it is reserved strictly for gold and silver jewelry under national BIS frameworks.

requirements.detail: Polyaluminium Chloride conforming to the quality and performance requirements of this standard must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's licence number (CM/L) printed clearly on each packaging bag or container.

Liquid PAC must contain a minimum of 9.5% Al2O3 (Medium Basicity) or 10.2% Al2O3 (High Basicity) by mass. Powder PAC must contain a minimum of 28.0% Al2O3 for both types. Relative basicity must be a minimum of 35% for Medium Basicity PAC and a minimum of 64% for High Basicity PAC.

Maximum chloride limits (as Cl) are: Liquid (12.5% Medium, 10.5% High); Powder (37.5% Medium, 31.0% High). Maximum sulphate limits (as SO4) are: Liquid (2.7% Medium, 2.5% High); Powder (10.0% Medium, 10.0% High).

The specific gravity at 25°C of liquid PAC must be a minimum of 1.18 (Medium) or 1.20 (High). Liquid dynamic viscosity at 20°C must fall within the range of 3 to 10 mPa.s. Bulk density for powder forms must be at least 0.65 g/ml.

To prevent water contamination, toxic trace impurities are strictly restricted. Maximum allowed thresholds are: Mercury (0.2 ppm liquid / 0.6 ppm powder); Arsenic (5 ppm liquid / 15 ppm powder); Lead (30 ppm liquid / 90 ppm powder); Cadmium (6 ppm liquid / 18 ppm powder); Iron (80 ppm liquid / 240 ppm powder); Manganese (20 ppm liquid / 60 ppm powder); Chromium (15 ppm liquid / 45 ppm powder); and Selenium (8 ppm liquid / 24 ppm powder).

requirements.requirement_type: Total Organic Carbon and Insolubles Restrictions
requirements.detail: Total Organic Carbon (TOC) is limited to a maximum of 80 ppm for liquid and 240 ppm for powder. Insoluble matter must not exceed 0.5 percent by mass for liquid or 1.50 percent by mass for powder.
The pH of a 5 percent solution must be: Liquid (1.8 to 4.5 for Medium, 2.5 to 4.5 for High); Powder (2.5 to 4.5 for both).

Liquid PAC must be colourless to pale yellow, hazy to transparent liquid, and Powder PAC must be pale yellow powder. Both forms must be completely free from odour, dirt, visible impurities, and foreign matter.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 15573 : 2018 is the strict national Indian Standard specification governing Polyaluminium Chloride (PAC), a highly effective chemical coagulant extensively used in municipal drinking water treatment, wastewater purification, and industrial water processing. Under the national Quality Control Order (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, all Polyaluminium Chloride manufactured or imported in India must be certified under the BIS Standard Mark scheme (ISI Mark). The standard covers liquid and powder forms of PAC, categorized by Medium and High Basicity. It enforces strict physical-chemical limits—including minimum Al2O3 concentrations, specific gravity, and viscosity—and sets very low maximum limits on heavy metals (such as lead, mercury, and arsenic) and organic carbon to ensure the safety of public water supplies. Amendment No. 3 (February 2026) updates the standard visual characteristics of the liquids and powders and corrects test references to Annex C.
